subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: Should Linux Quick Chat load arbitrary remote `http:`/`https:` agent-avatar URLs, including URLs that may reach private-network hosts, or should it accept a narrower trusted avatar-source policy?
rationale: This is a user privacy and network-trust decision, not a mechanical correctness choice; the branch deliberately widens CSP to support remote avatar rendering.

options.title: Adopt a narrow avatar-source policy
options.body: Restrict Quick Chat rendering to data/local-derived avatars and any explicitly approved remote scheme or host policy, with focused tests for allowed and rejected sources.

options.title: Accept arbitrary remote avatars
options.body: Keep unrestricted `http:`/`https:` image loading and explicitly document that configured agent identity avatars may trigger remote requests from the Linux companion.

options.title: Defer remote avatars
options.body: Keep the agent switcher but render only emoji or monograms until a repository-wide avatar loading policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow avatar-source policy
recommendation.body: Restrict Quick Chat rendering to data/local-derived avatars and any explicitly approved remote scheme or host policy, with focused tests for allowed and rejected sources.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing Linux Quick Chat path and authored the branch that expands its avatar and webview behavior.
